notes: Not launched on any device. SLUS-20018 is identified through Redump (USA disc 3769; Original and Greatest Hits share the serial) and the PCSX2 GameIndex.

PCSX2 GameIndex SLUS-20018 at commit b3402c13 (2026-10-21) gives compat 5. In PCSX2's GameDatabase.h enum that means 'Playable'; 6 is 'Perfect'. The entry also sets gsHWFixes texturePreloading 1 and gameFixes SoftwareRendererFMVHack. This is desktop upstream data only.
The US manual says the left analog stick is not used; movement is D-pad only.
GameSpot's page now shows 'May 8, 2014' (an editor's note says only screens and video were updated). The 2001-03-09 date comes from the page's parsely-pub-date metadata.

IGN's 2001 review page is reachable only via Wayback; the on-page date is March 14, 2001. Wikipedia cites a separate Perry article dated 2001-01-25, probably the Japanese import coverage, which I didn't use. IGN's 2019 remaster score of 6.5 is taken from IGN's game hub and Wikipedia because ign.com returned 403. The in.ign.com mirror of that review shows a garbled 6.8 score and an unrelated verdict box.

The Issen mechanics in the article (soul multiplier, Hajiki Issen, lock-on quirk, the second Marcellus being the only boss that can be Issen-ed) come from a fan FAQ and are labelled as such. The US manual pages I inspected don't name Issen.
The Easy-mode unlock condition varies between fan guides (3 or 5 deaths, sometimes specifically against Osric). The article says only that it's hidden and that the guides disagree.
The Famitsu 35/40 score and the 'first PS2 million-seller' claim come from Wikipedia, not from the primary sources.

The ES-DE cover for 'Onimusha - Warlords (USA)' is actually the PAL box (ELSPA 15, capcom-europe.com), and the ES-DE screenshot is a composite 'mix' image that includes that PAL box. I used neither; the lead image is the libretro NTSC-U boxart instead.

Manual source date is given as year only ('2001', not full YYYY-MM-DD). The scan carries no printed date; I verified only that it's the 2001 NTSC-U PS2 manual, so I didn't use the March 14, 2001 release date as its publication date.

The manifest lead is a gameplay screenshot; the US box cover appears in the body after the first paragraph. A title-screen image was dropped from the pack; the Samuragochi credit is sourced to Wikipedia.

notes: Nothing was played or launched on any device.
PCSX2 compatibility (SLUS-21361 compat 5, eeRoundMode fix for a Mission 18 door) is desktop upstream data only.

libretro-thumbnails Named_Titles for the USA/EU/JP SE entries all serve the same French-language PAL title screen ('Edition Spéciale'), so it was not used. The libretro SE Named_Snaps (Vergil gameplay) was a lead candidate but the GameSpot SE screenshot is sharper and shows the style meter.
The style menu screenshot is from the original 2005 release, and the caption says so. SE keeps the same four starting styles, but the SE menu itself was not separately captured.

Mission grades are described as 'from D upward' on purpose. Wikipedia lists S and SS as top marks, and Dahbomb's FAQ mentions an 'SS rank' run on Dante Must Die, which corroborates SS. The wording is still conservative.

Itsuno's reasoning on styles is reported second-hand through producer Matt Walker (USgamer 2020). A 1UP 'Postmortem on DMC3:SE' interview (James Mielke) cited by Wikipedia for Vergil's cut moves could not be fetched (archive.today timed out; Wayback 404), so the article makes no claims from it.
A fan-wiki claim that Itsuno named each style after a fighting game (e.g. Royal Guard after Street Fighter III's parry) has no primary source and was left out.
Whether cutscenes can be skipped was not verified and is not claimed.

Steam availability resolved. The issue editor checked the Steam appdetails API on 2026-10-24: success true, the HD Collection (which includes DMC3 SE) has an active US purchase package. The 2023 GameSpot 'retired on Steam' headline wasn't read (403), and what it covered is unknown. The article doesn't claim the standalone 2006 PC port is available, and leaves out the price because it changes.

Style levelling: the article says only that the four starting styles level up. Wikipedia (Vergil's style 'leveled-up twice like Dante's four styles') and Screen Rant's 2020 levelling guide describe levelling only for the four starting styles plus Dark Slayer. No primary source was found on whether Quicksilver and Doppelganger level, so the article doesn't say either way.

Locked-on roll input R1 + left/right + X comes from Dahbomb's GameFAQs FAQ; GameSpot 2005 confirms a wrong direction makes Dante jump. Starting weapons (sword plus twin handguns) come from GameSpy 2005; the names Rebellion and Ebony & Ivory from the FAQ and Wikipedia.

notes: Nothing was played or tested on any device. The availability section lists official releases only and makes no emulation claim for the 360 or PS3 discs.

Medal scale: the BradyGames tables rate each verse criterion (time, combo, damage) from Bronze to Platinum. 'Pure Platinum' as a higher verse grade comes from the GameSpot (360) and Eurogamer reviews, not the guide or manual. Stone is the manual's lowest chapter trophy. I didn't verify whether a verse itself can score Stone, so the article doesn't say so.

Bat Within: the guide says 'press RT immediately after taking damage ... mitigating any damage you've take[n]'. The article repeats 'mitigates' and doesn't claim full negation, because the guide doesn't specify it.

Climax Brace: the guide's unlock table lists 'obtain 101 Umbran Tears of Blood -> enter Shop'. No alternate unlock was checked, so the article says the guide lists that condition and doesn't use 'only'.

Screenshot platform: GameSpot published all three images in its Xbox 360 review under its 360 product ID (946346). The pixels can't prove the capture hardware, so every caption reads 'supplied with GameSpot's Xbox 360 review; capture platform not independently verified'. MobyGames 360 screenshots weren't used because Cloudflare blocked both a scripted fetch and a headless browser.

The mechanics come from the PC (Steam, 2017) manual and the BradyGames guide, not the 2010 Xbox 360 manual. Control descriptions use 360 buttons (RT evade, LT weapon swap), which match the PC manual's gamepad layout.

The PS3 port credit: Nex Entertainment lists BAYONETTA on its archived consumer-works page without naming a platform. Platinum's Minami (via Digital Foundry) says only that Sega did the port. The article says Nex 'is credited with' the port and does not claim more.

Edge: the review is unsigned. The issue number E209 comes from Wikipedia's Edge 10/10 list, and the 10/10 is confirmed by the ratingValue markup in a 2014 Edge Online capture; the 2010 capture's text doesn't print the number.
1UP's grades (X360 A, PS3 A-) come from the 1UP page sidebar. The reviewer's name (Matt Leone) appears only on Wikipedia, so the article doesn't name a reviewer.

The QTE criticism is attributed to Wikipedia's reception summary. The lethal-QTE example (Route 666, Jump prompt) comes from the official guide. No contemporary pro review quote on QTE deaths was located.
The guide's date is inferred as c. 2010; no date is printed in the scan.
Umbran Climax is deliberately not mentioned because it is a Bayonetta 2 mechanic. Kamiya's 'Mommy Mode' remark was not used.
